page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a shared, burstable virtual instance designed for entry-level workloads with intermittent compute demands. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data, and the baseline network bandwidth is designated at 0 Gbps. Dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.t5-c1m4.large across the lowest percentiles for compute and memory throughput due to its shared and throttled burstable baseline. It scored 1057.79 in single-core and 2090.03 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 870.0 and multi-core score of 1493.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 16.3 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 14.44 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific measurements reflect these hardware limitations, delivering 2.54 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 1.48 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 23.72 tokens per second for small 135M model LLM text generation.

The shared resource allocation model provides an economical footprint for applications that do not require sustained compute performance. However, severe CPU throttling under continuous utilization makes it unsuitable for compute-intensive pipelines or high-throughput production environments. The instance is best suited for low-traffic web services, non-critical background jobs, code repositories, staging environments, and entry-level development servers.

Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 2 vCPUs across a single hyperthreaded core paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage with a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Across synthetic and practical benchmarks—including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark—it consistently scores in the lower tiers due to CPU credit and sharing limitations. It achieves 2.54 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 1.48 GB/sec in static web serving. Given its burstable baseline, this configuration is cost-effective for non-continuous, low-utilization tasks, making it suitable for development sandboxes, staging systems, light administrative tooling, and intermittent background tasks.
